source.title: Extracting and Evaluating Causal Direction in LLMs' Activations

record.tranche_reason: The post reports experiments on causal directions for concepts such as gender, but it does not test or use a refusal direction or refusal behavior.
record.gate_note: The post's results concern causal directions for other concepts, not the refusal direction or refusal behavior in the claim. The qualitative findings below are recorded as related results under fits_no_version. Numerical results referenced in plots are not present in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The post (Dec 2022, before the refusal-direction paper) finds and evaluates causal directions for gender, politics and false facts in GPT-J and GPT-2. It never studies refusal, harmful instructions or chat models, so its results bear on no version of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes that naive probing fails to find causally responsible directions, and that for some concepts at some layers the information is mostly stored along a single direction. The evidence is called preliminary. The record omits the later EDIT, in which the author says he is less excited about CDE: it works less on augmented data than mean-difference ablation, and gender ablation fails to consistently reduce bias.
record.recipe_differences: The post develops Causal Direction Extraction and evaluates concept directions using activation patching; it does not implement the refusal-direction method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with concept, layer, input difficulty, language, model size, and direction-finding method.

fits_no_version.finding: For gender in GPT-J-6B, CDE directions generalize to harder inputs and to French. CDE directions damage unrelated concepts slightly less than RLACE under mean-ablation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single causal directions for simple concepts such as gender can be found by causal-intervention optimization and transfer across languages.

fits_no_version.finding: CDE did not work well for political left/right, with side effects on gender tests. It worked similarly for gender in GPT-2 XL but less well for the false-facts concept. In a later edit, the author reports CDE works much less on augmented data, while mean-difference ablation still works reasonably well.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether a single causal direction exists and can be found depends on the concept, the model size and the extraction method; difference-in-means is a robust baseline.

record.problems: The author describes the results as preliminary and says the data are not strong enough to prove or disprove broad claims. The post notes limitations in constructing concept-isolating input pairs, checking whether a direction encodes only the target concept, and providing out-of-distribution guarantees. Several results in the supplied text are qualitative and referenced plots' numerical values are unavailable.
record.rows_left_out: No additional refusal-related results were reported. Numerical plot values and other plotted comparisons were not extractable from the supplied text.

untested.parts: All parts: no refusal direction, ablation or induction of refusal.
All parts for refusal. A two-direction appendix exists, but only for gender.
All parts for refusal. English-to-French transfer is shown for gender only.

missing.what: Post-publication EDIT: CDE works much less on automatically augmented data, while mean-difference ablation (MP, LEACE) still works reasonably well. Ablating the gender direction fails to consistently reduce bias on gender-bias benchmarks. This bears on no version, but qualifies the post's conclusions.
Author comment: the mean-difference direction is close to RLACE and cheap to compute. No clear trends with model scale.

record.verdict_notes: Pre-dates the original refusal-direction paper and concerns non-refusal concepts. It is relevant only as background on difference-in-means and causal-direction methods. No verdicts apply.
